display.title: Reb Meir Refoels and the Agunah
display.summary_short: An agunah, sent by the Alter Rebbe to the Vilna community head Reb Meir Refoels, refuses to give up until he finds her missing husband among a group of prisoners.
display.summary_long: In the days of the Alter Rebbe, a Chassid brings his daughter to the Rebbe in Liozna. Her husband vanished three years ago, and as an agunah she can neither find him nor remarry. After deep thought, the Alter Rebbe tells her to go to Vilna, to Reb Meir Refoels, head of the community and one of the chief opponents of the Chassidim, and not to let go of him until he helps her. The Chassidim collect money for her journey. Reb Meir's wife scolds her for coming, and Reb Meir tells her it is impossible, but her bitter tears win a promise, and she waits at the guest house and reminds him every day while the town laughs. Reb Meir is a wealthy man with friends in the police, and he often frees Jews arrested for living or trading where Jews were not allowed. When a group of Jewish prisoners arrives, he finds her husband's name on the list. The man will not answer, but she recognizes him at once, and he agrees to give her a get in exchange for his freedom. All of Vilna gains respect for the Alter Rebbe, and Reb Meir begins to wonder whether he should become a Chassid; another miracle, for another time, will decide it.
display.lesson: A tzaddik's ruach hakodesh sees what others cannot; trust his words and keep trying.

advisories.note: A husband abandons his wife for three years; she receives a get at the end.
Jewish prisoners facing exile to Siberia for breaking residence laws.

quality.notes: No opening song; told in a scripted, storybook style ('Kinderlach'). Ends by promising the second story 'some other time'.
